title: Spinal Epidural Abscess: Red Flags, MRI and Emergency Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with suspected spinal epidural abscess (SEA) in the emergency department (ED) or ward: red flags in back pain, urgent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), cultures, empirical antibiotics, and same-day neurosurgical referral for neurological deficit. Uses the MSD (Merck) Manual 2025, the NHS Lothian community spondylodiscitis antimicrobial guideline 2024 and product labels. Children and post-operative wound infections are excluded.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi or national SEA guideline was found; the main clinical source is a professional reference (tier 3), labelled as such.

Empirical antibiotic choice differs: MSD Manual names vancomycin with ceftriaxone; NHS Lothian (spondylodiscitis) names flucloxacillin 2 g every 6 hours with vancomycin for severe penicillin allergy; flucloxacillin label was not opened. See comparison.
Regimens after neurosurgical or urological instrumentation (ceftazidime, cefepime or meropenem with vancomycin) are named by MSD but no labels were opened, so doses are not listed.
Gram-negative cover in severe beta-lactam allergy was not sourced; discuss with microbiology.
Typical normal ranges for white cells, C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate are not from these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: SEA arises by blood spread (endocarditis, skin boil, dental abscess) or direct spread (vertebral osteomyelitis, pressure ulcer, retroperitoneal abscess); a third have no cause found (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology). Staphylococcus aureus caused about 60% of cases in one series; Gram-negative bacilli and streptococci are next (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology). The abscess compresses the cord or roots, so deficits progress over hours to days (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs). Most occur in the thoracic or lumbar spine (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).

symptoms: Severe local or radicular back pain, sometimes worse lying down (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).
Fever (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).
Leg weakness, saddle numbness, bladder or bowel dysfunction (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).
physicalSigns: Focal spinal percussion tenderness (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).
Leg weakness and saddle anaesthesia (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).
Abnormal neurological examination (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Escalation).
redFlags: Any neurological deficit (weakness, bladder or bowel dysfunction): immediate surgical drainage (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).
Back pain with fever, focal tenderness or risk factors: consider immediate MRI even without neurological signs (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).
Haemodynamic instability, abnormal neurology or imaging showing SEA: involve microbiology and neurosurgery (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Escalation).
Do not do lumbar puncture: risk of cord herniation (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).
precipitants: Injection drug use (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).
Bacteraemia from instrumentation or dental procedures (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).
Endocarditis, boils, dental abscess (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).
Vertebral osteomyelitis or pressure ulcer (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).
Tuberculosis (Pott disease) (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Etiology).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Disc involvement (discitis) favours abscess over tumour on imaging (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).

differentials.condition: Vertebral osteomyelitis or spondylodiscitis without abscess
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No epidural collection on MRI (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Escalation).

differentials.condition: Cauda equina syndrome from disc prolapse
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No fever or infection markers; MRI shows disc (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Symptoms and Signs).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Epidural collection with or without discitis or osteomyelitis
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: The diagnostic test; arrange immediately for unexplained back pain with focal tenderness or risk factors (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect and examine
actions: Ask about fever, injection drug use, recent procedures and infections; examine spine, power, sensation including saddle area, and bladder function (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Sections Etiology and Symptoms and Signs).

clinicalManagement.title: Image urgently
actions: Request urgent MRI of the spine (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).
Take 2 sets of blood cultures before antibiotics (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Investigations).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer to neurosurgery
actions: Any deficit: immediate surgical drainage (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).
Discuss every confirmed SEA with neurosurgery and microbiology (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Escalation).

clinicalManagement.title: Start antibiotics
actions: Unstable or neurological deficit: start empirical antibiotics after blood cultures without waiting for tissue (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).
Stable, no deficit: obtain deep samples before antibiotics where this does not delay care (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Investigations).

clinicalManagement.title: Directed therapy and follow-up
actions: Narrow therapy to culture results with infection specialists; usually 6 to 12 weeks (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Duration).
Repeat neurological examination often; urgent MRI and neurosurgical review for any new deficit (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).

regimens.indication: Empirical cover for Staphylococcus aureus including methicillin-resistant strains in spinal epidural abscess
regimens.dose: Adults: 2 g per day as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours, each over at least 60 minutes (Vancomycin label, Section Dosage and Administration); local practice doses by calculator to a trough of 15 to 20 mg/L (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Penicillin allergy). PAEDIATRIC: 10 mg/kg every 6 hours (Vancomycin label, Section Dosage and Administration).
regimens.frequency: Every 6 or 12 hours, adjusted to levels
regimens.duration: Until culture results; total therapy usually 6 to 12 weeks as directed by infection specialists (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Duration)
adjustments: Renal impairment: daily dose in mg is about 15 times the glomerular filtration rate in mL/min; first dose not below 15 mg/kg (Vancomycin label, Section Dosage and Administration).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Vancomycin levels (trough 15 to 20 mg/L locally) (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Penicillin allergy).
Renal function in all patients; risk of acute kidney injury rises with exposure (Vancomycin label, Section Warnings).
Hearing in prolonged therapy (Vancomycin label, Section Warnings).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to vancomycin (Vancomycin label, Section Contraindications).
Infuse over at least 60 minutes to reduce infusion reactions (Vancomycin label, Section Dosage and Administration).

regimens.indication: Empirical cover for streptococci and Gram-negative organisms in SEA
regimens.dose: Usual adult dose 1 to 2 g once daily or divided twice daily; maximum 4 g daily (Ceftriaxone label, Section Dosage and Administration). PAEDIATRIC serious infections: 50 to 75 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours, maximum 2 g daily (Ceftriaxone label, Section Dosage and Administration).
regimens.duration: Until culture results, then as directed
adjustments: No adjustment in renal failure alone or hepatic dysfunction alone; with both, do not exceed 2 g daily (Ceftriaxone label, Section Dosage and Administration).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Encephalopathy or seizures, mostly in severe renal impairment (Ceftriaxone label, Section Warnings).
Gallbladder or urinary sludge symptoms (Ceftriaxone label, Section Warnings).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or any cephalosporin; higher risk with previous penicillin hypersensitivity (Ceftriaxone label, Section Contraindications).
Do not mix or give with calcium-containing intravenous solutions in the same line (Ceftriaxone label, Section Warnings).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: MRI showing epidural collection; computed tomography (CT) myelography if MRI is unavailable (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Diagnosis).
Neurological compromise such as paresis or bladder or bowel dysfunction (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).
No neurological deficit: antibiotics with or without CT- or fluoroscopy-guided aspiration (MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment).

guidelineComparison.title: Empirical antibiotics for spinal infection

values: Flucloxacillin 2 g intravenously every 6 hours; add gentamicin if Gram-negative risk

guidelineComparison.note: Both shown; agree the regimen with microbiology. MSD Manual SEA 2025, Section Treatment; NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Sections Empirical therapy and Penicillin allergy.

teaching.scope: Adults with suspected spinal epidural abscess (SEA) in the emergency department (ED) or ward: red flags in back pain, urgent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), cultures, empirical antibiotics, and same-day neurosurgical referral for neurological deficit. Uses the MSD (Merck) Manual 2025, the NHS Lothian community spondylodiscitis antimicrobial guideline 2024 and product labels. Children and post-operative wound infections are excluded.
learningObjectives: Spot SEA red flags in back pain.
Get urgent MRI and blood cultures.
Refer any neurological deficit for immediate drainage.
pitfalls: Discharging back pain with fever without imaging.
Starting antibiotics before cultures in a stable patient.
keyPoints: Fever plus back pain plus tenderness needs MRI.

patientEducation: This is an infection pressing on the spinal cord; treatment may need surgery and weeks of antibiotics.
Report new weakness, numbness or bladder problems immediately.
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid injecting drugs; seek help from addiction services if needed.
mdtReferrals: Emergency physician; neurosurgeon; infectious diseases and microbiology; radiology; physiotherapy; outpatient antibiotic team.
dischargeCriteria: Neurology stable or improving, organism known, antibiotic plan and outpatient intravenous or oral switch agreed, follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Infection clinic and neurosurgery review during the 6 to 12 week course (NHS Lothian spondylodiscitis 2024, Section Duration).
